help_detail_update:
*/update* — Update containers by name or glob

`/update <name>` — check + update one container (if it has an update).
`/update <glob>` — update every matching container that has a pending update, e.g. `/update gluetun-*`.

📌 Runs a check first, then applies only matching containers with updates — same path as the Update-all button (group order, dependents cascade, health-check + rollback). Typing the pattern is the go-ahead, so no extra confirm. Use `/check <glob>` first to preview.

*/protect* — Protect a container from Stop

`/protect` — list protected containers.

📌 A protected container has no Stop button (Telegram + Web UI) and Stop is refused — so you can't accidentally take down something you depend on, like the VPN/tunnel carrying your remote access. Restart and updates still work. Also settable on the container detail page in the Web UI.

*/cooldown* — Per-container update cooldown

`/cooldown` — list containers with a cooldown set.

help_detail_status:
*/status* — Container overview

`/status` — list of all containers (running + stopped) with health icons, uptime and image.
`/status <name>` — full detail for one container: state, health, ports, volumes, restart policy, plus inline action buttons (Update / Restart / Stop).

📌 Partial name matches work: `/status jelly` resolves to `jellyfin` if unambiguous.
help_detail_check:
*/check* — Trigger an update check now

Forces an immediate scan instead of waiting for the next `CRON_SCHEDULE` tick. Compares the local image digest of every running container against the registry. Pending updates land in a new "🔄 Updates Available" notification with one-tap buttons.

⚠️ Refuses while an update is already running (race-lock since v1.18.9).
help_detail_updates:
*/updates* — Show pending updates

Lists every container Docksentry has previously flagged as having an update available, with action buttons. Equivalent to re-displaying the last "Updates Available" notification without re-running the check.

📌 Empty when nothing is pending.
help_detail_cleanup:
*/cleanup* — Remove unused Docker images

Removes images older than `CLEANUP_GRACE_HOURS` (default 24h) that no running container references. Set `CLEANUP_BACKUP_LOCAL_ONLY=true` to back locally-built images up as tarballs first (in `/data/backups/`).

⚠️ Side effects: posts a notification, frees disk. Check before / after with `/status`.
help_detail_lifecycle:
*/start /stop /restart* — Single-container lifecycle

`/start <name>` — start a stopped container
`/stop <name>` — stop a running container (refuses on self for safety)
`/restart <name>` — stop + start in one shot

Partial name matches work. Stop refuses on the Docksentry container itself.
help_detail_maintenance:
*/maintenance* — Pause scheduled checks

`/maintenance <duration>` — silence auto-updates for the duration (e.g. `2h`, `30m`, `1d`, `forever`).
`/maintenance off` — re-enable immediately.
`/maintenance` (no arg) — show current state.

📌 Manual `/check` and `/update` still work during maintenance. Only the cron-driven auto-update is paused.
help_detail_history:
*/history* — Recent update history

Last 20 update events (success + failure) with date arrows, image size deltas and version arrows when the upstream image carries an `org.opencontainers.image.version` label. Includes self-updates of Docksentry itself since v1.17.6.
help_detail_pin:
*/pin /unpin* — Skip / re-enable updates for a container

`/pin <name>` — exclude from update checks (won't appear in `/updates`)
`/unpin <name>` — re-include
`/pin` (no arg) — list pinned

📌 Useful when you want to stay on a specific image version without env-var pinning.
help_detail_autoupdate:
*/autoupdate* — Toggle silent auto-update for a container

`/autoupdate <name>` — flip auto-update on / off for that container
`/autoupdate` (no arg) — list containers with auto-update enabled

📌 Auto-updated containers don't generate a "Updates Available" prompt — they run on the next cron tick with no button-tap needed. Use carefully: combine with `restart_dependents` Container Groups when a container has sidecars.
help_detail_setlink:
*/setlink* — किसी कंटेनर का रेपो / चेंजलॉग लिंक सेट करें

`/setlink <नाम> <url>` — लिंक सहेजें (पूर्ण `http://` या `https://` URL होना चाहिए; बाकी सब अस्वीकार होगा)
`/setlink <नाम>` (बिना url) — हटाएँ और लेबल आधारित पहचान पर लौटें

📌 कंटेनर लेबल `docksentry.link` इस कमांड पर भारी पड़ता है — इसे अपनी compose फ़ाइल में रखें, लिंक कंटेनर के साथ चलेगा।
📌 यह लिंक `/changelog` के आउटपुट, अपडेट सूचनाओं के रेपो लिंक और वेब UI के 🔗 आइकन — तीनों को चलाता है। तब उपयोगी जब अपस्ट्रीम इमेज `org.opencontainers.image.source` OCI लेबल सेट नहीं करती।
help_detail_audit:
*/audit* — Inspect-coverage audit for a container

`/audit <name>` — run the v1.19.0 audit logger against this container's `docker inspect` and report any HostConfig / Config fields that are non-default but NOT restored on recreate.

📌 If the output is empty, you're safe — every important field is preserved. If anything shows up, please file an issue with the lines so we can extend coverage.
help_detail_selfupdate:
*/selfupdate* — Update Docksentry itself

`/selfupdate` — pull `:latest` and recreate (helper-container swap)
`/selfupdate <X.Y.Z>` — pin to a specific version (e.g. `/selfupdate 1.19.0`)
`/selfupdate previous` — roll back to the last released version older than the running one

📌 Different code path than container updates — `selfupdate` uses a helper container to swap PID 1.
help_detail_changelog:
*/changelog* — What's new

`/changelog` — list Docksentry releases newer than the running version, with links
`/changelog <name>` — show the repo / changelog link for one container

📌 We don't try to fetch and parse arbitrary container changelogs (formats vary too much) — for containers we point you at the upstream source repo.
help_detail_debug:
*/debug* — Toggle debug logging

`/debug` — flip debug on / off. When on, internal events (cron ticks, network attach, audit-mode warnings, container resolve hits) appear in `docker logs docksentry`.

📌 No impact on Telegram chat output — only on host-side logs.
help_detail_logs:
*/logs* — Show recent container logs

`/logs <name>` — last 30 log lines from the container, formatted as a code block.

📌 Useful right after an update report: `❌ jellyfin: …rolled back` → then `/logs jellyfin` to see what crashed.
help_detail_lang:
*/lang* — Switch the bot language

`/lang en` or `/lang de` — change to English or German. Other 14 languages fall back to English strings (translation contributions welcome).
`/lang` (no arg) — show current language.
help_detail_settings:
*/settings* — Current configuration

Shows the active schedule, language, auto-selfupdate flag, healthcheck max-starting wait, debug state and other env-driven settings. Read-only via Telegram; the Web UI lets you edit most of these without restart.
help_detail_help:
*/help* — Command reference

`/help` — list of all commands with a one-line summary
`/help <command>` — detailed help for a specific command (synopsis, parameters, examples)

📌 The autocomplete picker (type `/` in this chat) is faster for discovery — try it.
audit_usage: Usage: `/audit container_name` — checks the container's inspect for fields we don't restore on recreate.
audit_clean: ✅ `{name}`: clean — every non-default HostConfig and Config field is restored on recreate.
audit_findings_header:
🔍 *Audit for* `{name}`:

The following fields are non-default in your inspect but NOT restored by `_build_run_args`. On recreate they'd be silently dropped.
audit_footer: 📬 Please [open an issue](https://github.com/amayer1983/docksentry/issues) with this list so we can extend coverage.
web_groups_page_intro: Manage VPN-sidecar / shared-namespace stacks here. The first container in a group is the *head* — when it's updated, dependents are restarted (if you enable `restart_dependents`). Drag rows to reorder.
web_groups_head_tt: The head container — when it's updated, the rest of the group reacts (restart, recreate, etc).
web_groups_stale_tt: This container no longer exists on the host. Edit the group to remove it.
web_groups_drag_tt: Drag to reorder. The first one is the head.
web_groups_no_members: No containers in this group yet.
web_groups_autodetect_intro: Each card is a detected stack (containers grouped by `com.docker.compose.project` or `com.docker.stack.namespace`). Check the ones you want to import as Docksentry groups. Drag rows inside a card to set the head order before importing.
web_groups_autodetect_none: No Compose / Portainer / Swarm stacks detected on this host. Stacks need the standard project labels — manual `docker run` containers can't be auto-detected.
web_groups_autodetect_conflict: ⚠ Already in group `{group}` — will be moved on import.
web_groups_autodetect_skip_existing: Stack already imported (group exists with same name)
data_loss_alert:
⚠️ *No persisted settings found* — possible data loss.

Your Telegram config came from env vars, but `/data/settings.json` is missing. Container groups, pin / autoupdate / link / window state may have been lost too. Common causes: host reboot mid-write (fixed in v1.22.0 with atomic writes — won't happen again), volume mount missing at start, fresh `/data/` volume.

If you have a backup, restore via Web UI → Settings → Import. Otherwise re-configure and check the Web UI's Status page for any groups / pins you'd set up.
storage_wrong_mount:
⚠️ *Your data directory is not where you think it is*

`{source}` is mounted at `{dest}`, but Docksentry never reads or writes there — its data lives in `{data_dir}`. So that directory stays empty, and everything Docksentry saves goes to an anonymous volume that is thrown away the next time this container is recreated: by `compose down`/`up`, by a `docker rm`, or by a self-update.

Fix the mount and the losses stop:

`- {source}:{data_dir}`

Restore your last backup afterwards (Web UI → Settings → Import) — this time it will stay.
storage_anonymous:
⚠️ *Nothing here survives a recreate*

`{data_dir}` is an anonymous volume — Docker made one because nothing was mounted there. It is a fresh one for every container, so settings, groups and pins are discarded the next time this container is recreated: by `compose down`/`up`, by a `docker rm`, or by a self-update.

Mount a directory or a named volume at `{data_dir}`, for example:

`- ./docksentry-data:{data_dir}`
storage_unmounted:
⚠️ *Nothing here survives a recreate*

Nothing is mounted at `{data_dir}`, so everything saved there lives inside the container itself and goes when the container goes — on `compose down`/`up`, on a `docker rm`, or on a self-update.

Mount a directory or a named volume at `{data_dir}`, for example:

`- ./docksentry-data:{data_dir}`
web_backup_intro: Export every persisted setting (groups, notes, links, pins, autoupdate flags, update windows, webhook URLs, etc.) into a single JSON file. Restore it later — useful before host migrations, or just as defense-in-depth against data loss.
web_backup_hint: Backups contain webhook URLs and bot tokens — treat the file like a password. The import path skips unknown keys, so forward-compatible if a future Docksentry adds new settings.
update_snapshot_stale_msg: ⚠️ That "Updates Available" notification is too old to act on (a newer check has replaced it, or the bot restarted). Run /check for a fresh list.
selfupdate_old_tag:
✅ The `:{current}` image tag is up to date — but that's a *fixed version*, and a newer release (`v{latest}`) exists. Your container won't move past `:{current}` on its own. To upgrade:
• `/selfupdate {latest}` (jump to the new version), or
• `/selfupdate latest` (rejoin the rolling latest line), or
• set `image: amayer1983/docksentry:latest` in your compose and `docker compose up -d`.
policy_held: ⏸ `{name}`: held back by update policy ({level} {old} → {new}). Run /update {name} to apply, or set docksentry.policy=all.
age_held: ⏳ *{name}*: अपडेट रोका गया — नई इमेज {days} दिन पुरानी है, यह कंटेनर {required} दिन प्रतीक्षा करता है। लगभग {remaining} दिन में स्वतः लागू होगा।
web_check_one_tt: इस कंटेनर के लिए अभी अपडेट जांचें
web_check_one_busy: इस समय एक अपडेट चल रहा है — थोड़ी देर बाद फिर कोशिश करें
web_selfupdate_marker_tt: Docksentry खुद को AUTO_SELFUPDATE से अपडेट करता है, कंटेनर-वार ऑटो-अपडेट सूची से नहीं — इसे सेटिंग्स › Updates में बदलें।
web_selfupdate_settings_tt: सेल्फ-अपडेट सेटिंग्स › Updates में सेट होता है — वही पेज खुलेगा।
web_detail_selfupdate_hint: Docksentry केवल AUTO_SELFUPDATE के ज़रिए खुद को अपडेट करता है; कंटेनर-वार ऑटो-अपडेट सूची उस पर लागू नहीं होती। स्विच सेटिंग्स › Updates में है।
web_update_tt: नई इमेज खींचकर इस कंटेनर को दोबारा बनाएँ — वॉल्यूम, पोर्ट, नेटवर्क और एनवायरनमेंट बने रहते हैं।
web_pin_tt: मौजूदा इमेज पर पिन करें — अनपिन करने तक अपडेट जाँच इस कंटेनर को छोड़ देगी।
web_unpin_tt: पिन हटाएँ — यह कंटेनर फिर से अपडेट जाँच में शामिल होगा।
web_restart_tt: इस कंटेनर को पुनः आरंभ करें — वही इमेज, वही कॉन्फ़िगरेशन, बस थोड़ी देर की रुकावट।
web_stop_tt: इस कंटेनर को रोकें — जब तक कोई इसे दोबारा शुरू न करे यह बंद रहेगा; डेटा और कॉन्फ़िगरेशन सुरक्षित रहते हैं।
web_link_open_tt: इस कंटेनर का रेपो / चेंजलॉग पेज नए टैब में खोलें
web_link_origin_registry: इमेज नाम से अनुमानित — रजिस्ट्री का सामान्य पेज, चेंजलॉग नहीं
web_link_cleared: लिंक हटा दिया गया — स्वतः पहचान फिर से लागू है।
web_link_rejected: लिंक अस्वीकृत: केवल पूर्ण http:// या https:// URL स्वीकार हैं, बिना स्पेस और उद्धरण चिह्नों के।
web_healthcheck_max_starting_hint: अपडेट किए गए कंटेनर को «healthy» रिपोर्ट करने के लिए अधिकतम समय, इससे पहले कि अपडेट विफल माना जाए और वापस रोल किया जाए।
web_docker_stop_timeout_hint: «docker stop» किसी कंटेनर के स्वयं रुकने के लिए कितनी देर प्रतीक्षा करता है, उसके बाद उसे बलपूर्वक समाप्त कर देता है।
web_monitor_hint: चल रहे कंटेनरों पर नज़र रखता है और जब कोई रुकता है, क्रैश होता है या unhealthy हो जाता है तो अलर्ट भेजता है।
web_monitor_interval_hint: कंटेनर स्थिति कितनी बार जाँची जाती है। न्यूनतम 15 सेकंड।
web_password_hint: इस इंटरफ़ेस पर HTTP Basic प्रमाणीकरण के लिए पासवर्ड। वर्तमान बनाए रखने के लिए खाली छोड़ें; नया पासवर्ड तुरंत प्रभावी होगा।
host_local_only_hint: ℹ️ Local host only — add `@<host>` or `@all` for the others.
help_hosts: /hosts — Show the hosts this instance manages
web_audit_intro: State-changing actions from the Web UI, Telegram, Discord and the scheduler. Secrets are never recorded.
monitor_oom_flag_yes: ⚠️ The kernel OOM-killed it — this was memory.
monitor_oom_flag_no: Not an OOM kill — the exit code came from something else.
startup_hard_kill: ⚠️ The previous run was killed rather than stopped — no clean shutdown was recorded. Exit 137 usually means the kernel or the runtime ended it: check host memory and CPU load around that time.
recovery_restored: 🔧 An update was interrupted mid-swap. {name} was left stopped under a backup name and has been restored and started.
recovery_stale: 🔧 An update to {name} was interrupted more than a day ago and `{old}` is still there. Not touched — too old to act on safely.
recovery_failed: ⚠️ An update to {name} was interrupted and `{old}` could not be restored automatically. It needs a hand.
recovery_gone: ⚠️ An update to {name} was interrupted and neither the container nor its backup is there any more.
web_badge_newer_tt: Pinned to {current}. Version {newer} exists on the registry — Docksentry will not switch to it, because the tag you pinned is what it keeps running. Change the tag in your compose file to move.
web_discord_bot_intro: वैकल्पिक, और ऊपर दिए वेबहुक से अलग। बॉट टोकन से Docksentry केवल सूचनाएँ भेजने के बजाय डिस्कॉर्ड में कमांड भी लेता है — /status, /update, /logs और 19 अन्य। एप्लिकेशन discord.com/developers/applications पर बनाएँ।
web_discord_token_help: अपने डिस्कॉर्ड एप्लिकेशन के Bot पेज से। settings.json में सहेजा जाता है, जिसे केवल उसका स्वामी पढ़ सकता है। सहेजा गया टोकन बनाए रखने के लिए खाली छोड़ें।
web_discord_token_clear_help: टोकन मिटाता है और बॉट रोक देता है। ऊपर का डिस्कॉर्ड वेबहुक अछूता रहता है।
web_discord_app_id_help: अपने डिस्कॉर्ड एप्लिकेशन के General Information से। आवश्यक — स्लैश कमांड इसी पर पंजीकृत होते हैं।
web_discord_guild_id_help: वह डिस्कॉर्ड सर्वर जिस तक बॉट सीमित है। आवश्यक। डिस्कॉर्ड में डेवलपर मोड चालू करें, फिर सर्वर के नाम पर दायाँ क्लिक करके Copy Server ID चुनें।
web_discord_allowed_users_help: वैकल्पिक — अल्पविराम से अलग किए डिस्कॉर्ड उपयोगकर्ता ID जिन्हें कमांड चलाने की अनुमति है। खाली छोड़ने पर ऊपर के सर्वर का कोई भी व्यक्ति चला सकता है।
web_discord_bot_started: डिस्कॉर्ड बॉट पुनः आरंभ हुआ और जुड़ गया।
web_discord_bot_off: डिस्कॉर्ड बॉट बंद है — इसके लिए बॉट टोकन और एप्लिकेशन ID दोनों चाहिए।
web_discord_bot_no_guild: सहेजा गया, पर बॉट शुरू नहीं हुआ: सर्वर ID नहीं है। वही बॉट को आपके सर्वर तक सीमित रखता है।
web_discord_bot_bad_token: सहेजा गया, पर डिस्कॉर्ड ने टोकन अस्वीकार कर दिया।
web_discord_bot_no_commands: बॉट जुड़ गया, पर स्लैश कमांड पंजीकृत नहीं हो सके। वे देर से दिख सकते हैं।
web_discord_bot_restart_needed: सहेजा गया। लागू करने के लिए Docksentry पुनः आरंभ करें।
web_discord_bot_error: सहेजा गया, पर बॉट शुरू नहीं किया जा सका।
web_connections_intro: Docksentry अपनी सूचनाएँ कहाँ भेजता है, और उनमें से कौन-सी कमांड वापस भेज सकती हैं। सेटिंग्स तय करती हैं कि Docksentry कब काम करे; यह पृष्ठ तय करता है कि वह कहाँ बोले।
web_conn_telegram_intro: बॉट टोकन और चैट ID पर्यावरण चर के रूप में सेट होते हैं। यहाँ जो है वह पहले से चल रहे बॉट पर लागू होता है।
web_conn_webhooks_intro: एकतरफ़ा सूचनाएँ। डिस्कॉर्ड सजाए गए ब्लॉक लेता है; सामान्य वेबहुक किसी भी स्वीकार करने वाले को JSON भेजता है।
web_conn_smtp_intro: ई-मेल से सूचनाएँ। सर्वर, प्रेषक और प्राप्तकर्ता सेट होते ही सक्रिय।
web_smtp_host_help: SMTP सर्वर का होस्टनाम या पता।
web_smtp_port_help: STARTTLS के लिए 587, SSL के लिए 465, बिना एन्क्रिप्शन वाले रिले के लिए 25।
web_smtp_tls_help: STARTTLS खुले कनेक्शन को उन्नत करता है; SSL पहले बाइट से एन्क्रिप्टेड होता है। „कोई नहीं“ सब कुछ खुले पाठ में भेजता है और केवल अपनी ही मशीन के रिले के लिए उपयुक्त है।
web_smtp_from_help: प्रेषक का पता। कुछ प्रदाता खाते के अपने पते के अलावा सब कुछ अस्वीकार कर देते हैं।
web_smtp_user_help: बिना प्रमाणीकरण वाले रिले के लिए खाली छोड़ें।
web_smtp_password_help: settings.json में सहेजा जाता है, जिसे केवल उसका स्वामी पढ़ सकता है। सहेजा गया पासवर्ड रखने के लिए खाली छोड़ें।
web_smtp_password_clear_help: पासवर्ड मिटाता है। बाकी ई-मेल सेटिंग्स बनी रहती हैं।
web_smtp_tls_verify_help: इसे चालू रहने दें। बंद होने पर पासवर्ड उस पते पर जो भी उत्तर दे उसे, किसी भी प्रमाणपत्र के साथ भेजा जाता है — इसे केवल स्व-हस्ताक्षरित प्रमाणपत्र वाले आंतरिक सर्वर के लिए बंद करें, और हर उपयोग पर यह लॉग में दर्ज होगा।
web_conn_ntfy_intro: ntfy के ज़रिए फ़ोन या कंप्यूटर पर पुश सूचनाएँ। या तो पूरा विषय URL, या सर्वर और विषय।
web_ntfy_url_help: पूरा, जैसे https://ntfy.sh/mera-vishay. यह भरें या नीचे के दो फ़ील्ड, दोनों नहीं।
web_ntfy_server_help: केवल सर्वर, जैसे https://ntfy.sh — नीचे के विषय के साथ।
web_ntfy_topic_help: उस सर्वर पर विषय का नाम। जो इसे जानता है वह आपकी सूचनाएँ पढ़ सकता है — कुछ ऐसा चुनें जो अनुमान से परे हो।

help_backup: /backup — Send a backup of settings, groups and pins as a file
help_detail_backup:
*/backup*

Builds the same bundle the Web UI exports — persisted settings, container groups, pins, auto-update flags, notes, links and update windows — and sends it into this chat as a file.

A copy is written to `/data/backups/` at the same time, and the five most recent are kept.

_The file contains your saved settings, which includes webhook URLs and the Web UI password hash. It goes to this chat only, but treat it the way you would treat the file itself._

help_detail_restart:
*/restart*

Stops Docksentry so its container's restart policy brings it back — which is how settings that only apply at boot take effect.

It checks that policy first. Without one, stopping would leave the container down and you without the bot you would use to bring it back, so it refuses and says so instead.

The next start knows it was asked for, rather than reporting an external stop signal.

hosts_single: This instance manages a single host.
restore_how:
📥 *Restoring*

Send the backup file into this chat — drag it in, or forward one from another Docksentry's chat. I will say what it contains and ask before changing anything.

Use `/backup` to get one.
help_restore: /restore — Restore from a backup file sent into this chat
help_detail_restore:
*/restore*

Send a Docksentry backup into this chat and I will offer to restore it. Dragging the file in is enough — the command itself only explains how.

Before anything changes you get told which instance the bundle came from, when it was made and what it would overwrite. The button is the decision, not the file arriving.

Unknown settings are dropped and links are checked, because a backup is a file and nothing about you picking it says you wrote it.
help_detail_hosts:
*/hosts*

Lists every host this instance manages and the endpoint it reaches each one through. On a single-host install it says so.

Useful when a check reports a host as unreachable: the endpoint here is the one that failed.
help_updateall: /updateall — Update every container with a pending update
help_detail_updateall:
*/updateall*

Updates everything currently listed as having an update, exactly like the *Update all* button under an update notification.

Pinned containers are skipped, groups are updated in order, and a failure stops that group but not the others.

help_detail_note:
*/note <container> [text]*

Attaches a short note to a container, shown next to it in the Web UI. Leave the text off to clear it.

For the things you will not remember in three months: why this one is pinned, which compose file it comes from, who else depends on it.
help_detail_trustrunning:
*/trustrunning <container>*

Some containers never report healthy — no healthcheck, or one that only passes under load. After an update Docksentry waits for health and rolls back when it does not come; for these, running is as good as it gets.

With this set, a container that is up but not green counts as a successful update. Without an argument it lists what is set.

Use it sparingly: it switches off the check that catches an update which started and then broke.
help_askmajor: /askmajor — Ask before applying a major update
help_detail_askmajor:
*/askmajor <container>*

A major version jump — 16 → 17 on a database, say — asks before it is applied rather than going ahead. You get the question with the update, and nothing happens until you answer.

Without an argument it lists what is set.
help_testchannel: /testchannel — Send a test notification to every channel
help_detail_testchannel:
*/testchannel*

Sends one message through every notification channel that is switched on — Telegram, Discord, e-mail, ntfy, Gotify, Matrix, Apprise, webhook.

More useful from here than from the Web UI: you are already standing where the message has to arrive, so "did it work?" answers itself. A channel that stays quiet is a channel to look at.
startup_killed_stopping: ⚠️ _The previous run was killed before it finished shutting down — `docker stop` ran out of patience and sent SIGKILL (exit 137). Nothing should be lost, every file is written atomically, but a longer `DOCKER_STOP_TIMEOUT` gives the web server, the scheduler and the Discord gateway time to come to a stop._
